new_candidates.body:
Hi!

I just stumbled upon the change in #1121, which broke a BT for us, but i'm not sure what the intended/correct behavior is. We have subtrees similar to this:

```xml
  <BehaviorTree ID="LogAndDoX">
    <Sequence>
      <Log mode_string="{mode}"/>
      <DoX mode_string="{mode}" />
    </Sequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
```

```xml
  <BehaviorTree ID="LogAndDoY">
    <Sequence>
      <Log mode_string="{mode}"/>
      <DoY mode_int="{mode}" />
    </Sequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
```

which we call like

```xml
<SubTree ID="DoX" mode="some_mode" />
```

and


```xml
<SubTree ID="DoY" mode="1" />
```

where `Log` has a string input, `DoX` has a string input, but `DoY` has an integer input.
Previously, both cases worked, but after the linked PR, the second case fails with the error `The creation of the tree failed because the port [mode] was initially created with type [int] and, later type [std::string] was used somewhere else.`.

Is there a recommended method of resolving a variable to the stringified version, or some other pattern usually used here? I could imagine something like 
```xml
  <BehaviorTree ID="LogAndDoY">
    <Sequence>
      <Log mode_string="{to_string(mode)}"/>
      <DoY mode_int="{mode}" />
    </Sequence>
  </BehaviorTree>
```
but can't find anything like that.
new_candidates.title: Question about automatic promotion of string to int in ports
